subject: Production: streaming output suppression causing client WS timeouts (BrightLeaf)
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@brightleaf.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brian Miller <brian.m@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [PROD] Generations stop streaming & client WS timeout spikes

Hi Dev,

We're seeing repeated events across several of our production clusters where the model starts streaming tokens and then goes silent for 7-12s before resuming (if at all). From the client's perspective the WebSocket session often ends with a timeout/connection-close after ~10s of silence, resulting in failed UX flows and high error rates.

Observations: 
- Starts happening at high sustained concurrency (~450-600 RPS across multiple sessions).
- Sporadic 504-like closes from our edge (we use Nginx LB).
- BrightLeaf saw a 6x increase in client-side reconnects and 3x higher visible error rate in the last 90 minutes.
- Attached a short server-side capture showing the chunked transfer halting (capture-20270618-ws-hang.log.txt).

This is hitting our customers; can you triage and advise immediate mitigation steps? We can open a war room and share credentials/traces.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Platform Engineer
BrightLeaf

Marissa — can you confirm what data you need (heap dump, perf counters, live pprof endpoint) and whether we can push a conservative config flip to increase chunk flush frequency?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [PROD] Generations stop streaming & client WS timeout spikes

Quick triage notes (preliminary):

- Reproduced a short run against BrightLeaf traffic shape in our perf lab. Under high multiplexing we observed a serialization pause when the KV cache eviction triggered while a session was mid-chunk. The runtime's chunk-assembler holds a lock while it merges persistent KV entries; eviction path can block the assembler for ~8-12s in the worst case.
- The pattern only appears when: HTTP/1.1 chunked + multiplexed sessions + high concurrent token-streams + aggressive eviction window (default for low-memory hosts).

Immediate mitigations I can push right now (no code change):
1) Increase WS keepalive/heartbeat on edge from 10s -> 30s so Nginx/LB doesn't prune mid-chunk. Command: nginx.conf: proxy_read_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 60s;
2) Force BrightLeaf routing to Dedicated pool that has relaxed eviction config (we can flip routing in the control plane).
3) Enable chunk flush micro-tuning: runtime config flag chunk.flush_interval_ms: 50 -> 20 (reduces chance of long gaps).

I will attach a short profiler snippet and the minimal checklist I ran. If we still see gaps after (1)+(2) we should consider a hotfix to the KV eviction path (low risk, small patch) — estimate 1-2 day PR and can be promoted through expedited pipeline.

Attaching: kb/initial-heap-profiler.txt and the diagnostic checklist.

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
